stories.title: Sierra Releases Personal Agent Protocol (Poppy) 1.0 — Live on Every Shopify Store and Meta Muse by Default
stories.body: Sierra released Personal Agent Protocol v1.0 (Poppy) on November 13, 2026, defining how a consumer's personal AI agent discovers a company and negotiates allowed actions through its website, APIs, or business agent. Every Shopify merchant in 175+ countries auto-publishes a Poppy file with no setup required, and Meta's Muse agent now calls Poppy on every site it visits by default. The design partner list passed 100 companies at launch, including Wayfair, Delta, Salesforce Agentforce, Cisco, and Synchrony.
stories.why: Any enterprise retailer now faces inbound traffic from personal AI agents operating on behalf of shoppers — Poppy sets the authentication and permission layer those agents use before they hit your commerce stack. A seller can use this to open a 'what's your Poppy strategy?' conversation with a CIO, directly linking the need for a governed context and identity layer to a live, shipping protocol.
stories.source_label: Sierra (official blog) / AI Weekly / Futurum Group

stories.title: Gartner Names Context Graphs a 'Peak' Technology in Its First Standalone Hype Cycle for Agentic AI (2026)
stories.body: Gartner's September 2026 report 'Context Graphs Ground AI Agents With Enterprise Knowledge' identifies context graphs as the foundational layer that grounds AI agents in declarative, procedural, and causal knowledge, with policies enforced through runtime constraints. The accompanying Hype Cycle for Agentic AI 2026 places context graphs at the Peak of Inflated Expectations, noting that unstructured RAG is insufficient for production agent deployments. Gartner predicts that by 2028 more than 50% of enterprise AI agent systems will leverage context graphs, driven by demand for greater agent autonomy.
stories.why: This is the highest-authority external validation a seller can cite for why a retailer must build a context/knowledge layer before agents deliver value — it reframes the conversation from 'AI tool' to 'missing infrastructure.' It also gives a rebuttal to any prospect that thinks RAG alone is enough to run enterprise retail agents at scale.
stories.source_label: Gartner (via Gartner.com abstract + Hype Cycle analysis)

stories.title: McKinsey & Gartner 2026 Data: Only 23% of Orgs Have Scaled Agents; 40%+ of Projects Face Cancellation by 2027
stories.body: A February 2026 roundup of analyst forecasts finds that agentic AI spending is projected to reach $201.9 billion in 2026 (Gartner), yet only 23% of organizations have scaled agent deployments according to McKinsey, and Gartner warns that more than 40% of agentic AI projects will be canceled by end of 2027. McKinsey's 'Merchants Unleashed' retail report finds that 71% of merchants surveyed say AI merchandising tools have had limited to no effect on their business so far, despite early adopters reporting significant revenue and margin lifts. Gartner's 2026 CIO Survey shows 17% of enterprises have deployed AI agents to date while 60%+ intend to within two years — a classic pilot-to-production stall pattern.
stories.why: The 71% 'no effect' statistic from McKinsey is a direct, citable answer to the objection 'we tried AI and it didn't work' — sellers can pivot to diagnosing why (data silos, no context layer) rather than defending the category. The 40% cancellation forecast from Gartner is an urgency tool: pilots that don't get the data foundation right now are statistically likely to be cut.
stories.source_label: Software Strategies Blog (citing Gartner, McKinsey) / Agxntsix (citing McKinsey 'Merchants Unleashed')

stories.title: BCG: Agentic AI in CPG–Retail Supply Chains Delivers +2–4% In-Stock Improvement and 60%+ Planning Productivity Gain
stories.body: A BCG Executive Perspectives report on supply chain published in May 2026 finds that agentic AI can boost in-stocks by 2–4% and planning productivity by more than 60% for CPGs and retailers by enabling synchronized, constraint-aware replenishment decisions between trading partners. BCG describes a CPG client that rebuilt replenishment using a modular agent backend, shifting from weekly batch cycles to continuous overnight evaluation of supply alternatives and service-level trade-offs. The report also flags that AI-related incidents rose 21% from 2024 to 2025, and that 69% of executives say agentic AI requires new governance structures.
stories.why: BCG's named outcome numbers (2–4% in-stock, 60%+ productivity) are boardroom-ready proof points a seller can drop directly into an ROI conversation with a supply chain or merchandising leader. The governance caveat — 69% of execs say agents need new controls — is a natural setup for why a governed context layer is prerequisite, not optional.

stories.title: Salesforce Acquires Intercom Fin; Decagon Hits $4.5B Valuation — Competitive Landscape Consolidates Around Outcome-Based Pricing
stories.body: Salesforce completed its acquisition of Intercom's Fin AI agent on September 10, 2026; Fin now operates inside Salesforce AI Labs while continuing to charge $0.99 per resolved outcome. Competitor Decagon, which serves Chime, Duolingo, Hertz, and Deutsche Telekom, reached a $4.5B valuation after a $250M Series D in January 2026 and was tracking approximately $100M in annualized revenue as of July 2026. Sierra, now valued at $15.8B and serving nearly half the Fortune 50, is priced at roughly $150K–$350K+ per year on an outcome basis — with no vendor in the category publishing a simple comparable enterprise price.
stories.why: Fin's move into the Salesforce orbit changes the competitive dynamic for any retailer already on Salesforce Service Cloud — sellers need to know whether Fin's $0.99 per-outcome model is a threat or a co-sell opportunity. The Decagon and Sierra valuation milestones signal that the enterprise market is validating outcome-based pricing, which is a useful anchor when discussing Graas's own commercial model.
stories.source_label: AI Magazine / getmacha.com (citing Salesforce acquisition data)
